chapter: Leaving St. Louis: Toby show, Darrell Harris and Eli Rice
title: Joining Eli Rice's band in Minneapolis
summary: Eli Rice paid $150, split with George Johnson, for the pair to join. He sang through a homemade five-foot megaphone, led a twelve-piece band, and Thomas stayed two or three years.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

we started traveling. So, ... we took a trip across the Erie, I think it was, and I met one of the great men of I thought I was going around the world. And ... music, Eli Rice.
What instrument did he play?
He sang. He had a microphone, I never seen one like it. It was personally made. It must have been I'd say around what they called in those day 5 feet tall. It was sort of/galvanized. Tremendous man.
When you say microphone, it was like a loud speaker or something?
No, it was one of those instruments like here. Now take this and turn this this other way and build it up to here where the voice can get through.
Like a megaphone.
Yeah and like a megaphone and get through there. Had a beautiful voice.
Was he a ballad singer? What did he sing, ballads?
He sing a bit of everything and he was very much loved in that part of the country.
How big a band was this?
Around 12 pieces.
Anyone else in that well-known besides you and George?
Yeah. Sure. Fellows like I'm selfish with the trumpets, you know.
Who?
JT (2 of 1) 83

I'm selfish about the trumpets. There was a fellow by the name of Eddie Thompkins. I thought he was a tremendous trumpet player. He worked with Lunceford's band here in New York. Tremendous trumpet player. And, Eddie Barefield.
Oh, I see. Yes.

I mean the fellows who came east, you know. Lot of fellows decided to stay out west. That's the story of lots of musicians because the city was (the bloom) they didn't want to get into. Like Dewey Jackson came here, he didn't want to be bothered. He wanted to turned around and/go back there. And, that's about -- no, Keg Johnson.
Oh, Keg was in there?
Oh, we got him later.
Well, how long did this go on with Eli Rice?
Well, I would say, Stan, around two or three years.
Oh, as long as that.
Yeah. We worked out of Minneapolis. He was the type of person who makes your decision, (?), he had a place to stay in, had some money in your pocket.
Well that was nice.
Tremendous.
